Statement B is not supported by current experimental evidence.  Work with both SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 ORF3a proteins shows activation not only of caspase-8 (extrinsic pathway) but also of mitochondrial (intrinsic) apoptotic signals, including changes in Bcl-2-family proteins such as Bcl-2 itself and activation of caspase-9.  Thus the claim that ORF3a “triggers caspase-8 … without affecting the expression levels of Bcl-2” and thereby acts only through the extrinsic pathway is incorrect.  

The other statements are consistent with present knowledge:
•  A – nsp10 binds the N-terminal ExoN domain of nsp14 to form the proofreading 3´-5´ exonuclease complex.  
•  C – Single-molecule studies show that SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 −1 PRF-stimulating pseudoknots can adopt (at least) two major conformations, and frameshifting efficiency correlates with conformational heterogeneity.  
•  D – −1 programmed ribosomal frameshifting at the slippery site/pseudoknot junction produces pp1a and pp1ab from the 5′ end of the genome, and the SARS-CoV-2 signal is structurally very similar to that of SARS-CoV.

Therefore, the only incorrect statement is:

Answer: B
